source_name: Nacionalni biro osiguravača Crne Gore (NBOCG) — National Bureau of Insurers, members and assembly
source_subtype: statutory industry bureau — member list + governance
why_relevant: Mandatory-membership body for all insurers in Montenegro; its Skupština president rotates among insurer CEOs (Matjaž Božić observed as assembly president c.2022). Because 'sector=both' includes bancassurance-linked payments and because NBOCG sits on the Chamber banking board, its member list and assembly elections extend the actor map to the insurance side.

source_name: Registar nevladinih organizacija (eNVO Registar), Ministarstvo javne uprave — NGO/association registry
why_relevant: Legally-mandated public registry: every association (including UBCG, ICT Cortex, AMM, MFIC, NBOCG, UPCG) must file its ovlašćeno lice za zastupanje (authorised representative) and report any change within 30 days. This makes the registry a lagging-but-authoritative confirmation channel for association leadership changes — and the advanced search enumerates any association matching banking/fintech keywords, i.e. it can discover bodies no news source mentions. 11,292 associations registered.

source_name: Bankar.me — Montenegrin banking trade press (association tag)
why_relevant: The most consistent reporter of association-level leadership events in this cell: it carried the Darko Radunović, Aleksa Lukić (Erste) and Tamaš Kamaraši (CKB, Sept 2025) UBCG board presidencies, the AMM digital-team launch and the CFO Association founding. Where association websites are stale or unresolvable, this tag feed is the working substitute and the discovery channel for new bodies.

source_name: Investitor.me — business/finance portal, association leadership coverage
why_relevant: Independently corroborated the same UBCG board-presidency transitions (Lukić 2021, Kamaraši 2025-09-18) with dated articles — a second-source confirmation channel for association leadership signals, reducing single-source risk on this cell.

source_name: Aktuelno.me — UBCG assembly and statute coverage
why_relevant: Carried the UBCG Skupština session adopting a new Statute and a 2026-2031 financial framework, and the expansion of UBCG's remit into digitalisation/AI, ESG, AML/CFT and financial inclusion — i.e. organisation-change signals about the association itself, which typically precede new committee/secretariat roles and hiring. Also named director Marija Šuković alongside assembly president Kamaraši.

source_name: MINA news agency — institutional/association wire
why_relevant: National agency wire that carried the UBCG statute/assembly item; agency copy is the earliest and most reliably dated version of association announcements and is syndicated onward, making it a good primary-timestamp source for leadership and organisational changes.

source_name: CompanyWall Montenegro — entity record for Udruženje banaka Crne Gore
why_relevant: Commercial registry aggregator carrying UBCG's registered address (Novaka Miloševa bb, Podgorica), founding date (2003-04-07) and contact details — useful for confirming legal identity, the registered representative, and for resolving the association's true web presence. Same pattern applies to every other association in this cell.

source_name: AmChams in Europe — member chamber directory
why_relevant: Umbrella directory that confirms AmCham Montenegro's canonical domain and its leadership contacts, and provides a stable resolution point if the national chamber's site is restructured. Low direct value, useful as a resolver.

source_name: Facebook / LinkedIn pages of Montenegrin industry bodies (UBCG via bankar.me, MFIC, UPCG, AMM, ICT Cortex)
why_relevant: For several of these bodies the social page is more current than the website — the observation that UBCG convened 'all 11 member banks' with a named director came from a Facebook post, and MFIC/UPCG/AMM LinkedIn pages announce board elections, new committee chairs and staff appointments before any press release. Practical fallback where association sites are stale or unresolvable.

source_name: INFINTECH Conference (Porto Montenegro) — speakers page
why_relevant: The single most important recurring banking/payments event physically held in Montenegro (Porto Montenegro, Tivat; editions 2024, 2025, 2026 on 8-9 October). Speaker cards carry full current job titles and employers for bank, fintech, regulator and telco executives across the Adriatic/Balkans, making it a dated, self-updating title registry. Observed entries include Ledia Bregu (Director of Payment Systems, Bank of Albania), Petar Stefanovic (Head of Digital Ecosystem and Cards Development, Moldinconbank), Andras Sebok (Deputy CEO Digital Division, OTP Bank), Piotr Jan Pietrzak (New Markets Lead, European Payment Initiative), and in the 2024 edition Danijela Vuksanovic (CMO, Addiko Bank Montenegro).

source_name: MFM Conference (Montenegro Financial Markets Conference), Hotel Hilton Podgorica
why_relevant: International financial-markets conference organised by the Capital Market Authority of Montenegro; the speaker roster is a dense, dated title registry of Montenegrin bank and regulator leadership. Observed 2025 entries: Tamas Kamarasi (President of the Management Board, CKB Bank), Mile Grbin (Member of the Management Board, CKB), Miljan Mijatovic (Director of Global Markets and Financial Services Directorate, CKB), Martin Leberle (President of the Management Board, NLB Banka), Zarija Milic (Member of the Management Board, NLB), Aleksandar Scekic (Head of Investment Banking, Erste Bank AD Podgorica), Gojko Maksimovic CFA (Director of Financial Markets Division, Hipotekarna banka), Irena Radovic (Governor, CBCG), Zorica Kalezic (Vice Governor), Biljana Gligoric (Advisor to the Governor for ESG and Innovation), Zeljko Drincic (President, Capital Market Authority). Visa was Platinum sponsor and Ana Draskovic (VP & GM Visa SEE) spoke — direct vendor-presence signal.

source_name: Bankar.me — KONFERENCIJE (Education > Conferences) section
why_relevant: The leading Montenegrin banking/finance trade portal maintains a dedicated conferences category that aggregates and reports on essentially every banking, payments, fintech and business event in the country, quoting speakers with their exact current titles. It is the fastest way to snowball to new event brands (Infintech, RE:D Montenegro, Tomorrow conference, AMM awards) and to catch one-off panels that never get a standalone website. Also runs interviews naming founders/directors and is itself a co-organiser (RE:D with Web Media Grupa, HESA Group and EBRD).

source_name: Asocijacija menadzera Crne Gore (AMM) — annual Najmenadzer / Manager of the Year awards
why_relevant: Montenegro's most prestigious national management award, under Government patronage. Citations name the winner WITH exact title and company, dated to the award year — a clean title-confirmation record for bank executives. Observed: 'Manager of the Year in Joint-Stock Companies' 2025 went to Lesia Vykhodtseva, Chairwoman of the Board, Zapad banka AD Podgorica; an earlier edition named Aleksa Lukic (Erste banka) as Najmenadzer. AMM also runs conferences and a 'digital committee' whose named membership reveals bank digital/IT leadership. President observed as Budimir Raickovic.

source_name: BIS Central Bankers' Speeches archive — Montenegro entries
why_relevant: Archives conference speeches by CBCG leadership with the speaker's exact official title, the event name, host, and date — a highly reliable, machine-readable confirmation layer for central-bank role changes and for identifying which regional banking/payments events Montenegrin officials attend. Observed: Irena Radovic's speech at the regional AML/CFT and anti-fraud for instant payments conference, Podgorica, 5 February 2026, attended by 40+ Western Balkans central bank representatives.

source_name: Euromoney Awards for Excellence — Montenegro national winners
why_relevant: Annual 'Best Bank in Montenegro' citation. The write-up is an editorially researched narrative that describes the winning bank's transformation programme (digital channels, payments infrastructure, core lending) and frequently names the CEO/management board members driving it — useful both as a title source and as a signal of which bank is investing in payments capability. Observed: NLB Banka named Montenegro winner for 2026; historically Erste Bank AD Podgorica (2014, 2017) and NLB in other years.

source_name: Global Finance Magazine — Best Bank Awards, Central & Eastern Europe (Montenegro)
why_relevant: Annual country award naming the best bank in Montenegro, plus separate Best Digital Banks in CEE, Best Consumer Bank and CSR categories. Award announcements are freely readable and are heavily amplified locally, with the winning bank's CEO quoted by name and title. Observed: CKB (Crnogorska komercijalna banka) named best bank in Montenegro for 2026 and winner of best consumer bank and best CSR bank categories; 33rd annual cycle.

source_name: The Banker — Bank of the Year Awards, Montenegro
why_relevant: FT-owned 'Bank of the Year' country award; historically the Montenegro title has gone to Erste Bank AD Podgorica (2011, 2013, 2016) and in recent cycles to CKB. Winners' write-ups and acceptance PR name the CEO/management board with current titles. Complements Euromoney and Global Finance so that a bank's leadership is confirmed by three independent annual cycles.

source_name: CBCG Annual Award (Godisnja nagrada Centralne banke Crne Gore) — laureates page
why_relevant: The central bank's annual scientific-work award publishes a dated list of laureates with their affiliations. It is a talent-pipeline registry rather than an executive registry: recipients are typically young analysts and academics who later appear in bank research, risk and payments departments, so it front-runs hiring. A 2026 competition round was announced.

source_name: Institut internih revizora Crne Gore (IIA Montenegro) — certification programmes and lecturer roster
why_relevant: Runs the 'Ovlasceni interni revizor' (Certified Internal Auditor) and an IS-audit specialist certification, plus conferences, seminars and workshops; affiliated with IIA and ECIIA Brussels. The 'Nasi predavaci' (our lecturers) page names trainers with their day-job titles — internal audit, risk and IT-audit heads inside Montenegrin banks are exactly the roles that show up there, making this a rare source of mid-level bank org structure that never appears in press releases.

source_name: Institut sertifikovanih racunovoda Crne Gore (ISRCG) — internal audit / professional certification
why_relevant: Professional body for accountants, auditors, valuers, internal auditors and forensics in Montenegro; publishes member and certification-holder information and runs continuing-education events. Useful for identifying finance/controlling staff inside banks and for spotting movement of CFO-track people, and its event speaker lists overlap with bank finance departments.

source_name: Crnogorski edukativni Centar Podgorica — trainers page
why_relevant: Commercial training provider in Podgorica whose 'nasi predavaci' page names instructors with their professional affiliations; commercial trainers in finance/compliance in a market this small are frequently serving or former bank staff, so the roster is a cheap secondary title source and a lead list for who is training bank employees.

source_name: Logate — INFINTECH organiser corporate site
why_relevant: Logate is the Montenegrin software company that organises INFINTECH; its role as organiser means its own site and the conference agenda pages together reveal both the local vendor ecosystem selling to banks and the partner/sponsor roster. Agenda pages carry per-session speaker titles that are more granular than the speakers index (session-level roles such as 'Head of Cards' surface here).

source_name: 10times — Budva / Podgorica / Montenegro event listings
why_relevant: Global event aggregator with country/city pages that list upcoming Montenegrin business, banking and technology events with dates, venues and organiser links. Best used as a discovery net to catch new or one-off event brands before they are covered by local media, then snowball to the event's own speaker page.

source_name: RE:D Montenegro conference (Web Media Grupa / bankar.me / HESA Group with EBRD)
why_relevant: New Montenegrin real-estate-and-finance conference co-organised by the bankar.me publisher with EBRD partnership. Real estate is where mortgage-lending and corporate-banking executives appear on panels, so the speaker list is a title registry for bank lending leadership. Observed speakers include Vasilije Jaukovic (Associate Director and Senior Banker, EBRD) and Milovan Novakovic (CEO & Partner, Colliers Montenegro).

source_name: Tomorrow Conference (Montenegro) — founder/organiser and speaker programme
why_relevant: Montenegrin business/technology conference brand (founder and director Mladjen Merdovic, per a bankar.me interview). Cross-sector conferences of this type routinely put bank digital and marketing leadership on stage with current titles, and their sponsor walls indicate which banks and payment vendors are spending locally.

source_name: Zene od uticaja (Women of Influence) business network — conference speakers page
why_relevant: Montenegrin business-network conference whose speakers page lists each speaker with exact organisation and title, including banking figures — observed: Jelena Vuletic (founder of Balance to Business and member of the board of Hipotekarna banka), alongside Nina Drakic (president, Privredna komora Crne Gore) and Tarik Zaimovic (executive director, ICT Cortex). Non-banking events like this are where board-level and second-line bank appointments surface without any bank press release.

source_name: Microfinance Centre (MFC) annual conference — Budva/Montenegro editions
why_relevant: The Microfinance Centre network holds its annual conference in Budva, Montenegro in some years, drawing MFI and bank inclusion/lending leadership from across the region with named agendas. Relevant to the non-bank credit segment (Monte Credit and similar) that sits alongside banks in Montenegro's payments and lending market.
